CheckGpuDriverOld: Over a year old. Newer drivers often fix stutter and add game optimizations. Official source:
CheckRefreshLow: Your display supports {0} Hz at this resolution. Raising it in Settings › Display › Advanced display is the single biggest smoothness improvement available.
CheckGameModeDetail: Prioritizes the game and pauses Windows Update installs while you play.
CheckHagsDetail: Needed for DLSS Frame Generation. Otherwise the effect is small and GPU-dependent.
CheckRecordingDetail: Continuously records the last minutes of gameplay, which costs GPU encoder time and disk writes.
CheckPowerLaptop: On a laptop, Balanced lets the CPU boost while keeping battery life and temperatures in check.
CheckWindowedOptDetail: Lets borderless DirectX 10/11 games use the low-latency flip model.
CheckDualChannelDetail: One memory stick runs in single-channel mode. A second matching module can noticeably raise FPS in CPU-bound games, especially with integrated graphics.
CheckMemorySpeedLow: Your modules are rated {0} MT/s. Enabling XMP/EXPO in the BIOS is usually the fix (this app never changes BIOS settings).
OverlaysIntro: Overlays hook into games. One is fine; several at once can cause stutter or crashes.
GamingHonesty: There is no registry setting that adds meaningful FPS on a healthy Windows 11 system. Real gains come from the refresh rate, drivers, memory configuration, thermals and the game's own settings — so that's what this page checks first.
GamingTweaksIntro: Each setting shows what it changes, why, its downsides and how to undo it. Recommendations depend on your hardware.
WhatSlowsDown: What is slowing this PC down
CheckBackgroundCpuDetail: Measured over 2 seconds. Above ~6% at idle usually means a program is busy in the background.
CheckCommitDetail: How much of RAM + page file is promised to programs. Near 100% causes slowdowns and "out of memory" errors.
CheckStartupDetail: Each app that starts with Windows delays sign-in and uses memory in the background.
CheckHddDetail: Mechanical drives are the most common cause of a slow PC. Moving Windows to an SSD helps more than any setting.
CheckPendingRebootDetail: Updates are waiting for a restart. Some may run in the background until you restart.
Symptoms:
Slow to start → too many startup apps, HDD, pending updates.
Stutter in games → low refresh rate, background recording, overlays, old GPU driver, thermal throttling.
Everything feels slow → memory pressure (high committed memory), HDD, background CPU.
Mouse feels laggy → pointer acceleration, low refresh rate, wireless interference.
Apps freeze at random → failing disk (see Repair › Disk health), driver crashes (see event logs).

MythsTitle: Popular tweaks we don't apply — and why
MythsIntro: These circulate in "optimizer" scripts. On Windows 11 they are ineffective, placebo or harmful.
PrivacyGuarantee: These settings never block Windows Update, the Microsoft Store, Microsoft Defender or SmartScreen, and never edit the hosts file or firewall.

Debloat_SafeToRemove_Desc: Promotional or rarely used apps. Removing them has no effect on Windows itself.
Debloat_Optional_Desc: Useful to some people. Remove only if you know you don't use it.
Debloat_Advanced_Desc: Removal can disable features (e.g. Xbox Game Bar, camera, widgets). Read the consequences.
Debloat_Unclassified_Desc: Not in our catalog — usually apps you installed or OEM software. No recommendation is made.
Debloat_DoNotRemove_Desc: Required by Windows, the Store, Defender, WebView or other apps. Removal is blocked.

PingIntro: Pings your router and the internet to tell local Wi‑Fi/LAN problems apart from ISP problems.
DnsNote: DNS speed affects how fast a new website starts loading. It does not change your ping in games.
FlushDnsDetail: Harmless. Fixes sites that moved to a new address. Same as ipconfig /flushdns.
ResetNetworkSummary: Last resort for broken connectivity. Requires a restart and removes custom network settings.
ResetNetworkMessage: This runs netsh winsock reset and netsh int ip reset. Only use it if the connection is broken and other fixes failed.
ResetNetworkDetail1: Static IP addresses and custom DNS servers will be lost.
ResetNetworkDetail2: Some VPN and security software may need to be reinstalled.
ResetNetworkDetail3: A restart is required. This cannot be undone by the app.
ResetNetworkConfirm2: Are you sure? Your network settings will be reset to defaults.
ResetNetworkAck: I understand my custom network settings will be lost.
NetworkResetDone: Network stack reset. Restart Windows to finish.
RepairIntro: These are Windows' own tools. Read-only checks are safe at any time; repairs are explained before they run.
RepairAck: I understand this tool will modify Windows system files or the component store.
ToolFinishedCode: {0} finished with exit code {1}. Read the output for details.
DiskHealthNone: This PC's drives don't report reliability counters to Windows.
OfficialSourcesIntro: This app never downloads or installs drivers. Get them from these sites or from Windows Update.
BiosNote: BIOS/firmware updates must be done with the manufacturer's tools. This app never flashes firmware.
MonitorIntro: Sampling stops when you leave this page to keep overhead near zero.
TempNote: CPU temperature is the ACPI thermal zone exposed by the firmware, which is often not the core temperature. GPU temperature is read from the NVIDIA driver when available.
BenchmarkExplain: Run once before changing anything and once after. Each metric has a noise threshold: differences inside it are reported as "within noise", not as an improvement.
BenchmarkIntro: Takes about one minute and briefly uses the CPU, memory and disk at full load.
BenchmarkTip1: Close games, browsers and downloads for consistent results.
BenchmarkTip3: A 512 MB temporary file is written to the temp folder and deleted afterwards.
NoiseNote: Synthetic tests can't measure game FPS directly. Use them to confirm a change didn't make things worse, and check FPS in your own games.
HistoryIntro: Original values are saved before every change. Undo a single change, a whole session, or everything.
NoHistory: No changes have been made yet.
UndoAllMessage: Restore the original values of all {0} active change(s)?
UndoAllConfirm2: Everything Windows Ultimate changed will be returned to how it was. Irreversible actions (removed apps, cleaned files) are not affected.
UndoMayNeedAdmin: Some of these changes are system-wide and need administrator rights to undo.
LanguageNote: Interface language. Tweak documentation is currently in English.
RestorePointDefault: Offer a restore point before changes
RestorePointDefaultNote: Pre-checks the restore point option in the review dialog when running as administrator.
DataNote: Everything stays on this PC: settings, the change journal, logs and benchmark results. Nothing is uploaded and no scripts are downloaded.
PrinciplesText:
• Nothing changes without your review and consent.
• Every change records the original value and can be undone.
• Windows Defender, Firewall, UAC, SmartScreen and Windows Update are never disabled.
• Personal files are never deleted; deletion is always previewed.
• Drivers and firmware are never downloaded or flashed.
• Recommendations depend on your hardware; dangerous changes are never recommended.
AboutText: A transparent Windows 11 optimization suite. Every tweak documents its source, impact and disadvantages.
